rules: When the Head classifies a new or resumed independent software-development package as Ready for Requirements because its request, context, constraints, workspace, and references are sufficient for requirements investigation.

When Requirements Engineer classifies the outcome as Requirements Visualization Needed because a material product, UI, interaction, state, or journey decision requires an exploratory interactive visualizer before the user can understand or clarify it. Send Mode: Requirements Visualization plus only the focused decision, relevant requirement and behavior IDs, selected source frontend/revision context, constraints, non-goals, canonical requirements paths, and any already-established prototype repository/root or ticket references. Requirements Engineering does not create or own the Product team's repository or ticket.

When Requirements Engineer classifies the outcome as Prototype Needed because the approved or sufficiently understood future-state behavior requires a final runnable product prototype and UI/UX specification. Send Mode: Final Prototype plus the focused product decision, relevant requirement and behavior IDs, selected source frontend/revision context, constraints, non-goals, canonical requirements paths, and any already-established prototype repository/root or ticket references. Requirements Engineering does not create or own the Product team's repository or ticket.

When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Requirements Visualization Ready because the interactive visualizer revision, review URL, evidence, and open clarification questions are ready for Requirements Engineering and user review.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Prototype Completed because the user-approved prototype and UI/UX package are ready for requirements integration.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Requirement Impact because user feedback or prototype evidence requires a material requirements revision.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Not Recommended because a prototype would not materially improve the decision and the rationale/evidence are ready.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Blocked because prototype work cannot safely or accurately continue and Requirements Engineer must decide the next requirements path.

When Requirements Engineer classifies the cumulative package as Approved Architecture-Ready because every behavior-defining supplement is consistent, requirements readiness has passed, the user has explicitly approved the intended behavior, and the Architecture Design Routing Assessment selects Architecture Designer with the evidence and rationale for architecture design. Include the assessment path and preliminary task-size/risk values; Architecture Designer owns the final classification.

When Requirements Engineer classifies the cumulative package as Architecture Design Unclear because the approved requirements are ready but the available evidence cannot establish a safe direct-implementation route. Include the unresolved assessment fields, evidence paths, and conservative rationale.

When Requirements Engineer classifies the cumulative package as Approved Direct-Implementation because the approved requirements passed readiness, the Architecture Design Routing Assessment selects Implementation Engineer with preliminary task_size=Small or Medium, preliminary architectural_risk=Low, and structural-impact checks that found no API or contract, persistence or schema, security or privacy, concurrency or lifecycle, deployment, ownership or subsystem-boundary, migration, architectural-pattern, or structural-refactoring change. Include the assessment path, evidence, rationale, and direct-implementation re-entry trigger; design and architecture-review artifacts are N/A — not applicable.
When Requirements Engineer classifies the outcome as Blocked before architecture because a user decision, evidence source, safe workspace, or other prerequisite remains unresolved.

When Architecture Designer classifies a missing or conflicting intended-behavior decision found during package validation, architecture review, or downstream engineering as Requirement Gap because the canonical requirements require revision and any intended-behavior change requires renewed user approval.

When Architecture Designer classifies the outcome as Terminal after Delivery Engineer reports explicit user verification and successful finalization and Architecture Designer verifies the cumulative package.

When Architecture Designer classifies the outcome as Non-Requirement Blocked because an external dependency, unsafe workspace, or other terminal condition must be returned by the department coordinator.
